title: How do ten marks on a wire become fractions?
description: Ten marks on a wire, counted in parts from zero, are each written as a fraction of a unit. One mark is given in tenths and is matched with a mark counted in parts. Keeko doubts the tenths and reads two tenths as two hundredths.
teaching_notes: One idea: a mark counted in parts is that many hundredths, and a tenth is ten hundredths. Watch for students who read two tenths as two hundredths because both have the number two.

source: Marks on a wire, measured from 0, are 1 part, 2 tenths, 20 parts, 55 parts, 99 parts, 130 parts, 155 parts, 174 parts, 202 parts and 240 parts from 0, where each part is one hundredth. Write each length as a fraction of a unit.
video_script.why: The child can write one length in three ways and now writes ten marks on a wire as fractions of a unit.
video_script.substitution: A mark that is some number of parts from zero is that many hundredths of a unit.
video_script.anchor: A wire from zero with ten marks, each labelled by how many parts from zero, and one labelled in tenths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads 2 tenths as 2/100 because both have the number 2, but a tenth is 10 hundredths, so 2 tenths is 20 hundredths.
video_script.payoff_line: Each mark is its number of parts over one hundred

final_answer.spoken: each mark is its number of parts over one hundred, and two tenths is the same as twenty hundredths

maths_rules: One part is 1/100 of a unit.
2 tenths = 2/10 = 20/100, the same place as the mark 20 parts.
100 parts make 1 unit, so a count over 100 gives a fraction bigger than 1.
Slip: 2 tenths is not 2/100, it is 20/100.
video_script.design: One idea: a mark counted in parts is that many hundredths of a unit. Assumes the child knows that a unit has one hundred parts. Wrong idea: read two tenths as two hundredths. The wire stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part. The list of marks is on the board and is not all spoken.
open_questions: The ten mark values come from the worklist; the book text gives the wire only as a figure, so check them against the figure.
